### Estimation

We can estimate $E[Y_i |  L_i = l , g_Y(\mathbf{L}, i) = l', A_i = a, h_Y(\textbf{A}, i) = a' ]$ non-parametrically by calculating the average of observations $Y_i$ for which $L_i = l$, $A_i = a$, $g_Y(\mathbf{L}, i) = l'$, and $h_Y(\textbf{A}, i) = a'$. The assumption of boundedness guarantees that as $n \rightarrow \infty$, we will get better estimates for each cell rather than a proliferation of cells to estimate.
